# PL-208 — Spectral-parameter-dependent resolvent transport is generic for bounded perturbation lattices

**Status:** negative result / programmability obstruction  
**Evidence class:** `EXACT-DERIVED + CLASSICAL-SECOND-RESOLVENT-IDENTITY + DECISIVE-NEGATIVE` for exact same-parameter left transport generated by bounded common-domain perturbations  
**Research line:** `prime_lattice`

## Claim

The spectral-parameter-dependent bounded transfer left open by `PL-206` and `PL-207` is not, by itself, a restrictive operator structure. On a broad class of self-adjoint prime-lattice families it is forced automatically by the second resolvent identity, and even its holomorphy, bounded invertibility, prime-square cocycle compatibility, off-axis norm control, and trace-class/finite-rank refinements can be completely generic.

Let `H` be self-adjoint on a Hilbert space and assign to each prime `p` an arbitrary bounded self-adjoint operator `V_p`. For every finite-support exponent vector `alpha`, define

\[
H_\alpha
=H+\sum_p \alpha_p V_p,
\qquad
R_\alpha(z)=(H_\alpha-z)^{-1}.
\]

Every `H_alpha` is self-adjoint on `Dom H`, so `C\setminus R` is a common resolvent domain. For one prime step set

\[
A_{\alpha,p}(z)
:=I-R_{\alpha+e_p}(z)V_p.
\]

Then for every nonreal `z`,

\[
\boxed{
R_{\alpha+e_p}(z)=A_{\alpha,p}(z)R_\alpha(z)
}
\]

and, more strongly,

\[
\boxed{
A_{\alpha,p}(z)
=(I+R_\alpha(z)V_p)^{-1}.
}
\]

Thus each transfer is bounded, boundedly invertible, and norm-holomorphic in `z`. Moreover

\[
\boxed{
\|A_{\alpha,p}(z)-I\|
\le \frac{\|V_p\|}{|\operatorname{Im}z|}.
}
\]

For distinct primes `p,q`, the transfers satisfy the exact noncommutative flatness relation

\[
\boxed{
A_{\alpha+e_p,q}(z)A_{\alpha,p}(z)
=
A_{\alpha+e_q,p}(z)A_{\alpha,q}(z).
}
\]

No commutativity of the operators `V_p,V_q` is needed. The equality is simply path independence of the resolvent attached to the common endpoint `alpha+e_p+e_q`.

If `V_p` is finite rank, then `A_{\alpha,p}(z)-I` is finite rank. If `V_p\in S_1`, then

\[
A_{\alpha,p}(z)-I\in S_1,
\]

and its Fredholm determinant is just the inverse of the ordinary perturbation determinant,

\[
\det A_{\alpha,p}(z)
=
\det(I+R_\alpha(z)V_p)^{-1}.
\]

Therefore the following package does **not** constitute arithmetic rigidity:

\[
\text{exact }z\text{-dependent transport}
+\text{ holomorphy}
+\text{ invertibility}
+\text{ prime-square flatness}
+\text{ off-axis control},
\]

nor does adding finite-rank or trace-class closeness to the identity rescue it. All of these properties can be manufactured from arbitrary bounded self-adjoint labels attached to the prime directions, with no use of `log p`, unique factorization beyond the indexing set, zeta continuation, or Riemann zeros.

The line-specific consequence is that the `A(z)` escape surviving `PL-207` must carry some **additional nonprogrammable arithmetic normalization or target coupling**. Spectral-parameter dependence and cocycle consistency alone are generic bounded-perturbation theory.

## 1. The second resolvent identity produces the transfer automatically

Fix `alpha,p` and write

\[
H_0=H_\alpha,
\qquad
H_1=H_{\alpha+e_p}=H_0+V_p,
\qquad
R_j(z)=(H_j-z)^{-1}.
\]

The second resolvent identity gives

\[
R_1(z)-R_0(z)
=-R_1(z)V_pR_0(z).
\]

Hence

\[
R_1(z)
=\bigl(I-R_1(z)V_p\bigr)R_0(z),
\]

which is exactly the claimed left transport with

\[
A(z)=I-R_1(z)V_p.
\]

The same bounded perturbation factorization also gives

\[
H_1-z
=(H_0-z)(I+R_0(z)V_p).
\]

Because both `H_0-z` and `H_1-z` are invertible for nonreal `z`, the bounded operator `I+R_0(z)V_p` is invertible and

\[
R_1(z)
=(I+R_0(z)V_p)^{-1}R_0(z).
\]

Thus

\[
A(z)
=(I+R_0(z)V_p)^{-1}
=I-R_1(z)V_p.
\]

In particular, the transfer is not an additional datum once the two neighboring Hamiltonians are specified: on this entire bounded common-domain class it is determined functorially by the ordinary relative resolvent formula.

This also reproduces exactly the propagation law in `PL-206`. Since

\[
A(z)-I=-R_1(z)V_p,
\]

Hilbert's resolvent identity gives

\[
A(z)-I
=\bigl[I+(z-w)R_1(z)\bigr](A(w)-I).
\]

So the `PL-206` constraint is not merely compatible with bounded perturbations; it is the standard resolvent propagation of the fixed perturbation `V_p`.

## 2. Self-adjointness supplies a common spectral domain and tame bounds

For each finite-support `alpha`, the perturbation

\[
\sum_p\alpha_pV_p
\]

is bounded and self-adjoint. Hence `H_alpha` is self-adjoint on the same dense domain as `H` and

\[
\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb R
\subset \rho(H_\alpha)
\]

for every lattice vertex.

For nonreal `z`, the standard self-adjoint resolvent bound gives

\[
\|R_{\alpha+e_p}(z)\|
\le |\operatorname{Im}z|^{-1}.
\]

Therefore

\[
\|A_{\alpha,p}(z)-I\|
=\|R_{\alpha+e_p}(z)V_p\|
\le \frac{\|V_p\|}{|\operatorname{Im}z|}.
\]

Since resolvents are norm-holomorphic on their resolvent sets, so is `A_{alpha,p}(z)`. Thus analyticity in the spectral parameter and ordinary upper/lower-half-plane growth control are not restrictive extra hypotheses either.

The construction is already maximally non-arithmetic at this stage. The labels `V_p` may be chosen independently and need not commute. The prime names can be replaced by any countable set of generators. Hence none of these properties distinguishes the rational primes from a matched free commutative-semigroup control.

## 3. Prime-square cocycle flatness is also automatic

The most natural attempted repair is to demand compatibility jointly across different prime directions rather than inspect each edge separately. But the elementary commuting squares of the exponent lattice still impose no rigidity on the present construction.

Applying the edge relation twice along the path `p` then `q` gives

\[
R_{\alpha+e_p+e_q}(z)
=A_{\alpha+e_p,q}(z)A_{\alpha,p}(z)R_\alpha(z).
\]

Taking the path `q` then `p` gives

\[
R_{\alpha+e_p+e_q}(z)
=A_{\alpha+e_q,p}(z)A_{\alpha,q}(z)R_\alpha(z).
\]

Subtracting,

\[
\Bigl(
A_{\alpha+e_p,q}(z)A_{\alpha,p}(z)
-
A_{\alpha+e_q,p}(z)A_{\alpha,q}(z)
\Bigr)R_\alpha(z)=0.
\]

The range of `R_alpha(z)` is `Dom H`, which is dense, and the operator in parentheses is bounded. Therefore it vanishes identically and

\[
A_{\alpha+e_p,q}(z)A_{\alpha,p}(z)
=
A_{\alpha+e_q,p}(z)A_{\alpha,q}(z).
\]

This is genuine operator-valued flatness, not scalar commutativity. Individual transfer operators need not commute, because the edge seen after moving in the other prime direction changes with the base vertex. Nevertheless every square closes exactly for arbitrary bounded self-adjoint `V_p`.

Thus even a noncommutative, vertex-dependent prime cocycle with exact path independence is insufficient as an arithmetic discriminator. A useful compatibility law must contain more than the tautological statement that all paths reach the same preassigned endpoint operator.

## 4. Trace-class and determinant refinements remain classical perturbation data

If `V_p\in S_1`, the ideal property gives

\[
A_{\alpha,p}(z)-I
=-R_{\alpha+e_p}(z)V_p\in S_1.
\]

Likewise finite-rank `V_p` gives a finite-rank transfer defect. Since

\[
A_{\alpha,p}(z)^{-1}=I+R_\alpha(z)V_p,
\]

the Fredholm determinant of the transfer is

\[
\det A_{\alpha,p}(z)
=\det(I+R_\alpha(z)V_p)^{-1}.
\]

This is precisely ordinary trace-class perturbation-determinant machinery. Multiplicativity of Fredholm determinants applied to the flat-square identity yields the corresponding scalar chain rule automatically. In the self-adjoint trace-class setting, boundary phases and spectral-shift functions are classical relative spectral data of the freely chosen perturbations.

This agrees with the earlier programmability audit around `PL-034`: trace-class comparability and perturbation determinants are not scarce enough to supply arithmetic rigidity. The present result is stronger in a different direction: before imposing `S_1`, **the exact spectral-parameter-dependent operator transport itself is already generic for arbitrary bounded perturbations**, and its joint prime-square consistency comes for free.

## 5. Prior art and novelty audit

The second resolvent identity, bounded-perturbation factorization, analyticity of the resolvent, and the self-adjoint estimate `||R(z)|| <= 1/|Im z|` are classical operator theory. Hilbert resolvent identities are reviewed, for example, in Leon A. Takhtajan, “Etudes of the resolvent,” *Russian Mathematical Surveys* **75**(1) (2020), 147–186, DOI `10.1070/RM9917`, arXiv `2004.11950`.

Trace ideals, Fredholm perturbation determinants, and their multiplicative properties are likewise classical Krein--Fredholm perturbation theory; no novelty is claimed for the determinant formula or chain rule. The current line already treats this machinery as classical in `PL-034`, `PL-206`, and `PL-207`, so no new `SOURCES.md` anchor is required for the elementary identities used here.

A targeted literature search around bounded perturbations, resolvent identities, perturbation determinants, and chain rules confirms that the mathematical ingredients are standard. The square-flat lattice organization above should therefore **not** be advertised as a new operator theorem: once the vertex family is preassigned, it is an immediate consistency consequence of the second resolvent identity.

The durable delta is line-specific. `PL-206` proved that a fixed same-parameter edge is trivial across a genuine resolvent family but retained a `z`-dependent edge as a formal escape. `PL-207` then closed fixed-edge spectral reparameterization and again left spectral-parameter-dependent transfer as one surviving architecture. The present finding shows that a very large and natural class of such `A(z)` families—including holomorphic, invertible, flat, finite-rank, and trace-class examples—is completely programmable from arbitrary bounded perturbation data. Therefore those structural adjectives cannot be the missing arithmetic input.

## 6. Adversarial boundaries

**Bounded common-domain perturbations are the scope of the construction.** The exact formula uses `H_{alpha+e_p}=H_alpha+V_p` with bounded `V_p`. Unbounded or domain-changing prime actions, boundary triples, extensions, and genuinely singular perturbations are not classified here.

**Flatness is only the ordinary square law.** The result does not rule out a stronger prime-indexed relation containing explicit arithmetic coefficients, a reciprocity law, a distinguished trace, a positivity constraint, or a coupling to a fixed target vector. It rules out treating path independence itself as such a relation.

**The `V_p` need not commute.** Commutativity of prime moves occurs at the level of the endpoint Hamiltonian because bounded operators add:

\[
H_\alpha+V_p+V_q
=H_\alpha+V_q+V_p.
\]

This algebraic equality does not imply `V_pV_q=V_qV_p`, nor does the proof use such commutation.

**Trace class is an optional strengthening, not a hypothesis of the main obstruction.** `S_1` merely places the already-generic transfer defect in the Fredholm-determinant regime. The result does not say that every target-relative trace-class invariant is programmable; it says that membership, determinant existence, and ordinary chain compatibility are not enough.

**No statement is made about zero localization.** The construction neither produces nor excludes Riemann zeros. Its role is negative: it shows that a candidate operator architecture can satisfy a surprisingly rich list of formal covariance properties while containing arbitrary non-arithmetic perturbation data.

**No claim of global uniformity in `p` is needed.** Each exponent vector has finite support and each step uses one bounded `V_p`. Uniform bounds over all primes would be an additional condition, but a bound such as `sup_p ||V_p||<infinity` can also be imposed on arbitrary matched controls and does not by itself introduce rational-prime arithmetic.

## Falsification / audit test

The main construction is falsified by any self-adjoint `H`, bounded self-adjoint family `{V_p}`, finite-support `alpha`, prime `p`, and nonreal `z` for which

\[
R_{\alpha+e_p}(z)
\ne
\bigl(I-R_{\alpha+e_p}(z)V_p\bigr)R_\alpha(z),
\]

or for which the displayed transfer is not equal to `(I+R_alpha(z)V_p)^(-1)`. Either would contradict the standard second resolvent identity and bounded perturbation factorization.

The square claim is falsified by a pair `p,q` for which the two ordered transfer products differ as bounded operators. But both products map `R_alpha(z)` to the same resolvent `R_{alpha+e_p+e_q}(z)`; their difference therefore vanishes on the dense range `Dom H`, forcing equality.

The **research conclusion**, rather than the operator identity, would be falsified by an RH-relevant theorem showing that one of the properties classified here—without any additional arithmetic normalization, target data, or source-specific hypothesis—excludes admissible non-Riemann matched controls. The arbitrary choice of `{V_p}` is the direct control against such an interpretation.

## Consequence for the research line

The exact-resolvent operator branch has now crossed a useful programmability boundary. `PL-206` and `PL-207` show that a spectral-parameter-independent bounded edge is too rigid; this finding shows that simply allowing the edge to depend on the parameter swings to the opposite extreme on bounded perturbation lattices: a holomorphic invertible transfer and its flat prime cocycle are automatic.

Accordingly, a new prime-lattice resolvent mechanism should not be promoted for merely exhibiting

\[
R_{\alpha+e_p}(z)=A_{\alpha,p}(z)R_\alpha(z)
\]

with analytic/invertible `A`, Schatten control, or commuting-square consistency. The arithmetic content must enter through an extra statement that arbitrary bounded perturbation lattices cannot satisfy: for example a source-forced normalization tied to `log p`, a distinguished target-relative matrix element, a global explicit-formula identity, a positivity/coercivity theorem, or another completion whose determinant or trace is not freely programmable.

That is the remaining testable operator frontier. Spectral-parameter dependence is scaffolding; the nonprogrammable arithmetic law, if one exists, has to do the real RH work.
